status.label: A Gold Coast group unheard overnight

headline: Flood-Net heard eight Gold Coast hinterland stations less overnight, but ARRO has their data: the gap was on our one route to them. Most checks came in.

scenes.title: Good morning
scenes.say: Good morning, Alex Chen presenting. Eighty-two percent of checks came in, up from seventy-eight. We stopped hearing twelve stations that keep a schedule; seven sit together in the Gold Coast hinterland, and they were reporting all along.

scenes.title: Unheard at night, Gold Coast hinterland
scenes.sub: eight stations, one way to us
scenes.say: Natural Bridge, Hotham Creek and Stewarts Road have been heard less at night most of this week. Last night we lost Binna Burra, Beechmont, Clagiraba Road, Willow Vale and Springbrook too, from half past two until five. Technicians found their data in ARRO: they were on the air. The gap is on our one route to them.

scenes.title: How Flood-Net hears them
scenes.say: It all reaches us one way: re-sent in ALERT2 by one concentrator, a station that gathers older-style reports and passes them on. Tallai's own reports thin out on that route too, so they can't tell Tallai from the route. Molendinar, same route, holds all night. No site visit needed.

items.text: Tallai AL: reaches us by the same route and thins out at night too; battery steady 13.4 V.
Molendinar AL, the same route to us: steady day and night.
ARRO has data from every station checked: they were on the air. The gap is between them and us.

scenes.title: Quiet in the Tweed and Richmond
scenes.say: Further south, we heard the Murwillumbah Hartigans Hill repeater once in the last day, just after noon Monday. Kunghur and Dunbible Creek are unheard too, but both have weak batteries, so not yet one cause. We lost Goonellabah, Terania Creek and Upper Burringbar together just before ten; ARRO will say if they reported. Tyalgum Creek had twenty millimetres of rain.

scenes.title: Our end of the line
scenes.say: Graham Watts, on the radio. Both receivers ran all day, no settings changed, and 152.400 still isn't listened to. One slow one: Bundamba Barclay Street's signal, measured on its own carrier, is down about three decibels in a week.

scenes.title: Batteries
scenes.say: The New Recruit. Is it supposed to do that? Hinze Dam read 9.1 volts last night after a week near 12.7, and Eungella fell from 10.9 to 9.5. One night each, so tonight will tell. Dunbible Creek is still 9.8.

items.name: Dunbible Creek at Dunbible Creek Rail Trail Bridge

scenes.title: Check signals
scenes.say: Turbo, quick lap! No checks heard from Boat Mountain, Rock Valley, Bromelton Dam or Blackstone Bridge. The gauge below Clarrie Hall Dam is still at zero.

scenes.title: That’s the network
scenes.say: That's the network: a Gold Coast group we heard less of, though ARRO has it all, two repeaters south we barely heard, and a hundred and twenty-three heard again. Back tomorrow.
scenes.line: That’s not a fault, that’s a symptom.

caveats: Corrected 3 Nov: technicians found the Gold Coast stations' data in ARRO, so they were reporting; the first version said they went quiet and pointed at Tallai.
Flood-Net hears that group only through one ALERT2 concentrator (11762) and one receiver; ARRO hears them by the Bureau's own routes.
Kunghur and Dunbible Creek have weak batteries of their own, so Hartigans Hill cannot yet be called their cause.
Hinze Dam's and Eungella's lows are single nights; one reading cannot separate a failing battery from a bad value.
author: Claude Code, from the draft and read-only queries; corrected 3 Nov
